entities.rationale: Stable and well run for its income, but succession after Kagame, the eastern Congo conflict and food insecurity in a dense, fast-growing population are the main risks; near-free essentials need a large outside boost.
One of the poorest countries, with a weak government, a history of civil war, very high fertility and most people without electricity; famine or renewed conflict is the main path to collapse.
Middle income and an energy exporter, but a deep currency and fuel crisis, political volatility, high debt and glacier loss threatening Andean water are the risks; weak institutions limit abundance.
Severe and worsening water stress, heavy dependence on imported energy and food, high debt and authoritarian drift are the risks; cheap solar and desalination are its best path.
Recurrent civil war, an almost non-functioning state, oil dependence and repeated famine make another multi-year loss of food or security for most people likely.
Rich, effective and peaceful, so collapse is mostly global risk; heavy energy imports, an aging population and health costs make near-free essentials unlikely without superintelligence.
Gangs control much of the capital, half the population is undernourished and the state barely functions, so a lasting loss of security or food for most people is about as likely as not.
Among the most water-scarce countries, dependent on imported energy and food, heavily indebted and next to regional wars; desalination plus cheap solar could fix water, but the fiscal strain is real.
Fast-growing and stable, so collapse risk is mostly global; hurricanes, imported energy, a heavy interest bill and poor water services hold back near-free essentials.
Rich, well run and an early AI adopter with ample energy, but total reliance on desalination and food imports in a hot, volatile Gulf, plus the end of oil income, are the vulnerabilities.
Gang violence, weak institutions, hurricanes and drought in the Dry Corridor are the main risks; low income makes near-free essentials a long shot.

The grid is failing, with island-wide blackouts and fuel and food shortages as imported oil shrinks, so a five-year loss of reliable electricity for most people may already be under way; a political or economic opening could reverse it.
Stable, effective and safe with low debt, so collapse is mostly global risk; aging and health spending keep essentials well above 10% of income without superintelligence.
Peaceful and well governed with strong solar and wind; rising drought, heat and the oldest population in this group are pressures, and near-free essentials depend on superintelligence.
Poor, authoritarian and dependent on remittances from Russia, beside Afghanistan and reliant on melting glaciers for water and hydropower; a messy succession or regional conflict is the main risk.
Weak state reach, tribal violence and high undernourishment are the risks, though plentiful water and subsistence farming cushion shocks; abundance is very unlikely.
Safe and rich enough to avoid collapse barring global catastrophe, but very high debt, water stress, heat and fires and an aging population make cheap essentials hard.
Oil and gas wealth and low debt give a buffer, but dependence on hydrocarbons, an authoritarian system, water stress and a volatile neighbourhood are the risks.
Rich, technologically strong and water-secure through desalination, but ongoing wars and regional nuclear rivalry make security the main risk, and defence spending keeps essentials costly.
A peaceful EU member with good access today; energy import dependence, high interest costs and weaker institutions slightly raise risk and lower the chance of near-free essentials.
